html:
The Sugaree were a small Native people of the Piedmont of the Carolinas, living along Sugar Creek near today's Charlotte, North Carolina. They probably spoke a Siouan language, like their powerful neighbours the Catawba.

Almost all that is known of them comes from the explorer John Lawson, who passed through their villages in 1701 and described their fields of corn. After the Yamasee War of 1715 and repeated epidemics, the small Piedmont peoples such as the Sugaree, Waxhaw and Eno merged into the Catawba Nation and disappear from the records as separate groups.
